Subject: Pricing exhibit redline: rephasing & clawback exceptions

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached is Brightline's proposed redline to the pricing exhibit (Brightline_Pricing_Redline_v2.pdf). A few high-level asks so you have context: 

- We need a formal one-time rephasing option in year 1 to account for our fiscal reorg (shifts ~30% of expected consumption).
- The clawback/true-up language as written would penalize short-term spikes driven by seasonal promotions or newly onboarded customers. We propose a carveout for one-off volume events and a smoothing approach over a 90-day rolling window.
- We're asking to cap any clawback at 25% of the quarterly invoice to avoid operational shock.

From a contracting perspective we'd like defined measurement windows, examples of what is considered an "exceptional spike," and clear ops steps so we can sign without leaving the finance team exposed.

Can Redwood propose precise language and any operational mitigations (e.g., escrow, staggered recovery) you would be comfortable with? Ideally we'd resolve this in the next two weeks so we can move to signature with the rest of the statement of work.

Thanks,
Sara

Team — forwarding Brightline's redline. Quick read and thoughts below (need legal + ops POV before we respond to Sara).

Proposal I'm inclined to offer (intro-level):
- Introduce a "tier-stitch" smoothing clause: measure committed vs actual on a rolling 90-day window, but allow one annual "rephasing" election in year 1 to shift up to one tier based on documented go-live changes.
- Replace hard "clawback" wording with a "true-up adjustment" that is applied over a 2-quarter recovery window, not a single immediate invoice.
- Cap true-up recoveries at 20% per quarter for a maximum of 40% over the 2-quarter recovery period (we absorb the remainder as a commercial concession).
- Add explicit exceptions for M&A, regulatory-driven volume changes, and force majeure-type marketplace events.

Why: keeps our unit economics intact, gives Brightline a runway to normalize, reduces risk of churn because of a surprise big invoice, and simplifies ops (we can amortize adjustments).

Open questions for Legal (Karthik): is language above defensible? Do we need escrow/holdback? For Ops (Laura/Markus): how hard is it to implement a 90-day rolling measurement and amortized recovery in our billing pipeline?

If we greenlight, I'll share a redline back to them that replaces clawback language and includes a mutual action plan (MAP) for rephasing requests.

Thanks — Priya

Priya — thanks for the ping. High-level legal take below; I'll follow up with tracked changes.

1) Terminology: prefer "true-up adjustment" over "clawback" — "clawback" reads punitive and may trigger revenue recognition and tax flags for Brightline (helps negotiations).

2) Measurement windows: define a primary measurement window (calendar quarter) and allow smoothing via a "rolling 90-day average" for the purpose of identifying spikes. Language should state: "A Spike is an increase in consumption that exceeds 200% of the trailing 90-day rolling average and is not attributable to Scheduled Campaigns, M&A, or regulatory requirements." Include examples in a schedule.

3) Recovery mechanics: propose amortized recovery across two subsequent invoices (quarterly) with a cap per invoice — cap at 20% is reasonable but I'd prefer 15% from a revenue predictability standpoint. If Commercial is comfortable with 20%, Legal can draft conditional fallback: 20% cap if Brightline elects to defer recovery to two quarters; otherwise 15% immediate.

4) Escrow/holdback: operationally heavy; recommend we only ask for escrow on deals > $X committed ARR. For this mid-market-sized deal, prefer amortization without escrow.

5) One-time rephasing election: allow a single rephasing request in year 1 subject to documented supporting materials (finance forecast, go-live logs) and mutual sign-off in the MAP. Limit to moving up no more than one tier or 30% of committed volume.

I'll attach a tracked redline (redlines_orderform.docx) with the above. Happy to join a call with their counsel if needed.

— Karthik

Priya / Karthik — operational notes from billing and revenue ops: 

- Implementing a 90-day rolling average is straightforward for consumption-tier mapping, but we need a mapping table that ties Brightline SKUs to our internal billing SKU. That table must be locked before any rephasing election can be processed.
- Amortized recovery (2-quarter) is doable but requires a special transaction type so finance can mark adjustments and avoid double-counting in recognition. We'll need the legal clause to specify exact recovery windows (e.g., "applied to the next two consecutive invoices following notice").
- One-time rephasing: we'll accept up to one rephasing in year 1, but only if the MAP includes specific evidence items (quarterly forecast, signed go-live checklist, customer success adoption report). 

I'll draft an ops playbook snippet to attach to the MAP that lists fields we need in the rephasing request and the SLA for processing (10 business days). Markus and I will scope the engineering work; estimate 2 sprints for automation if accepted.

Sara — thanks for the clarity and for sending the redline. We've reviewed internally and can agree in-principle to a middle-ground approach if Brightline accepts the following changes: 

1) Language swap: replace "clawback" with "true-up adjustment" and define a Spike as an increase >200% of the trailing 90-day rolling average, excluding Scheduled Campaigns, M&A, and regulatory-driven volume.
2) Recovery: amortized recovery across the two invoices immediately following notice; cap recoveries at 20% per invoice.
3) Rephasing election: Brightline is entitled to one rephasing election in year 1 to move up a single tier (max 30% shift) provided the rephasing request includes the evidence items listed in the attached MAP and is approved by both parties.
4) Exceptions: we will include carveouts for M&A and force majeure with examples in a schedule.

Next steps: I've uploaded a short Mutual Action Plan that outlines supporting docs and timelines (MAP_Brightline_Redwood_v1.gdoc). Please confirm by EOD Wednesday whether you can accept these mechanics and we'll send a tracked redline reflecting the exact clause language. If Brightline agrees, Karthik will share the redlined order form and Laura will attach the ops playbook for the billing steps.
